paragraphs: DNA sequences contain several kinds of structure at once: short local motifs, relationships between distant positions, and recurring patterns. The paper introduces the Synergistic Plasticity Unit, or SPU, to represent these patterns together. Its motivation is that static processing rules or an exclusive focus on sequence order can restrict how flexibly existing architectures capture DNA structure.

SPU combines three layers with distinct responsibilities. The Locus Plasticity Layer uses convolution operations tailored to individual tokens to capture local motifs. The Domain Plasticity Layer models sequence patterns alongside frequency patterns, bringing long-range and periodic information into global features. The Saliency Plasticity Layer then uses importance scores along two axes to regulate information flow through the model.

The contribution is the coordination of these mechanisms within one scalable architecture. The authors support the design with theoretical analysis, empirical evaluation, and biological interpretation, and report state-of-the-art performance with quasi-linear computational complexity. These findings suggest that adapting local processing, global representations, and information selection together can improve DNA modeling while keeping computational growth manageable.
icml-2026-adaptive-dna-sequence-modeling.tldr: SPU combines adaptive local processing, sequence and frequency modeling, and saliency scoring to improve DNA modeling with quasi-linear complexity.

paragraphs: Discrete diffusion models face a trade-off between understanding inputs and generating outputs efficiently. Masked diffusion language models perform well on semantic understanding and zero-shot generalization, while models using uniform noise offer strong generation with few steps. XDLM introduces a common framework intended to improve the balance between these capabilities.

The method connects both approaches through a stationary noise kernel, a rule governing the noise process. Its theoretical formulation includes masked and uniform-noise diffusion as special cases. An algebraic simplification of posterior probabilities also reduces a memory bottleneck. Together, these contributions provide both a unified account of the two approaches and a more practical way to implement their combination.

The experiments report an improved trade-off between understanding and generation. XDLM exceeds UDLM by 5.4 points on zero-shot text benchmarks and improves few-step image-generation FID from MDLM’s 80.8 to 54.1. Applied to an 8B-parameter language model, it reaches 15.0 on MBPP in 32 steps, approximately twice the baseline result. Training-dynamics analysis also suggests stronger potential for longer-term scaling.
icml-2026-balancing-understanding-and-ge.tldr: XDLM unifies masked and uniform-noise diffusion while improving the empirical trade-off between understanding and few-step generation.

paragraphs: A generative robot policy can represent several different ways to perform a task. Reinforcement learning can improve its success rate, but the improvement may come with a loss of variety: training can concentrate the policy on a single behavior that earns high reward. This paper addresses how to improve task performance while preserving multiple behavioral possibilities.

The proposed framework first discovers latent behavioral modes within a pretrained policy without supervised mode labels. These modes then support an intrinsic reward based on mutual information. This additional training signal encourages the discovered modes to remain informative about the policy’s behavior, giving reinforcement learning a reason to preserve distinctions between behaviors alongside its incentive to complete the task.

Experiments on robotic manipulation show higher success rates and richer action distributions than conventional fine-tuning approaches. The findings support treating behavioral diversity as an explicit training objective rather than assuming it will survive reward optimization. The paper’s contribution is a way to discover the relevant behavioral structure and use it to guide fine-tuning within the same framework.
icml-2026-behavioral-mode-discovery-for-.tldr: Discovering behavioral modes and rewarding their preservation improves robot-policy fine-tuning while retaining diverse actions.

paragraphs: Checking a mathematical proposition and finding an answer that satisfies mathematical conditions impose different demands. The paper argues that progress in formal theorem proving leaves constructive problem-solving underexplored. It introduces Formal Problem-Solving, or FPS, to bring answer construction and verification into one process in Lean 4.

FPS represents the unknown answer as a metavariable paired with a proof obligation. A solution must therefore supply an answer and establish that it meets the required conditions. The Deductive FPS framework organizes this work into forward derivation and backward verification, aiming to align formal solving more closely with human reasoning. The authors also introduce Restricted Propositional Equivalence, a symbolic correctness metric that looks beyond exact textual agreement.

Evaluation uses three benchmarks containing over 1,000 problems: FormalMath500, MiniF2F-Solving, and PutnamBench-Solving. Experiments with leading provers find that constructing solutions is substantially harder than proving propositions. This result identifies an additional burden in moving toward formally verified problem-solving: systems must discover appropriate mathematical objects while satisfying the logical constraints that certify them.
icml-2026-beyond-theorem-proving-formula.tldr: FPS connects answer construction with Lean verification and shows that formal problem-solving remains substantially harder than theorem proving.

paragraphs: Whole-slide pathology systems commonly summarize image patches, while pathologists also reason about individual cells. The paper argues that this mismatch reduces sensitivity to small lesions and subtle changes. Cello introduces cell-level representations into whole-slide analysis, with the aim of supporting both localized predictions and broader slide-level outcomes.

Cello learns cellular features using supervision from protein signals, preserving fine detail within the constraints of gigapixel images. For local tasks, a prototype-based contrastive module adapts representations to the task. For global tasks, gated aggregation learns from slide labels. A further consistency objective connects cellular evidence, local decisions, and global predictions so that these levels support a coherent decision process.

The authors report that Cello improves performance and exceeds state-of-the-art pathology foundation models pretrained on tens of thousands of samples, despite training with hundreds to thousands of samples. The stated contribution is therefore both representational and evidential: individual cells inform predictions, and the framework explicitly encourages agreement between the evidence used locally and the outcomes predicted globally.
icml-2026-cello-a-universal-cell-wise-fe.tldr: Cello combines cellular features with local and slide-level learning to improve pathology predictions and align their supporting evidence.

paragraphs: Conformal prediction and conformal risk control provide frameworks for quantifying uncertainty with formal guarantees in supervised learning. Applying them to generative systems is less straightforward because the established formulations do not directly accommodate tasks such as generating images or conducting conversations. Conf-Gen develops a general framework for bringing these methods into generative settings.

The approach adapts conformal risk control while relaxing its theoretical assumptions. It also places previous attempts to apply conformal prediction to language models within a broader formulation. This matters because the desired guarantee can concern different aspects of a system’s behavior, extending beyond the familiar supervised setting of predicting a label or numerical value.

The paper demonstrates applications involving guarantees about image generators producing non-memorized images, conversational systems having asked sufficient clarifying questions, and the correctness of agent outputs. These examples show the range of behaviors that the framework can address. The contribution is a shared uncertainty-quantification framework for such tasks; its stated conformal guarantees should not be read as a claim that every individual generated output is automatically correct.
icml-2026-conf-gen-conformal-uncertainty.tldr: Conf-Gen adapts conformal risk control to provide formal uncertainty guarantees for a broader range of generative tasks.

paragraphs: Explicit surface reconstruction turns a point cloud into a mesh describing a scene’s surfaces. Existing methods can produce strong reconstructions, but some spend several minutes optimizing each scene at test time. FastSESR targets that runtime bottleneck with a two-stage framework designed to produce scene-level meshes more efficiently.

First, a lightweight triangular candidate network identifies local connections among uniformly sampled points. Its representation factors triangle relationships through edges, supporting the extraction of candidate surface triangles. Second, an offset optimization network adjusts the geometry through a small, fixed number of learned updates guided by the candidate network. Learning these refinement steps moves work into the model instead of relying on a lengthy optimization process for each new scene.

Across multiple scene-level datasets, the authors report reconstruction at least 20 times faster than prior methods while retaining competitive quality. Shape-level evaluations also indicate good generalization. The findings support combining learned connectivity with learned geometric refinement as a practical route to faster reconstruction, without claiming that speed gains require superior quality on every benchmark.
icml-2026-fastsesr-fast-scene-level-expl.tldr: FastSESR uses learned triangle selection and fixed-step geometry refinement to reconstruct surfaces at least 20 times faster with competitive quality.

paragraphs: People who discover flaws in deployed AI systems can struggle to identify the right reporting destination and provide the information recipients need. Separate reporting forms create repeated work, while reports may remain isolated from other relevant organizations. FLARE-AI addresses this coordination problem through an interoperable reporting system.

The authors examine 12 existing systems and identify recurring challenges involving discoverability, reporting scope, information collection, coordination, and guidance for strict-liability cases. They combine this analysis with feedback from 49 experts across 32 organizations. The resulting design uses early classification and conditional questions to collect information relevant to assessing and prioritizing a flaw.

FLARE-AI produces standardized, machine-readable reports and allows optional distribution to multiple developers, coordinators, and incident registries from one submission. This connects report creation with the practical needs of recipients while reducing repeated form filling for reporters. The contribution is an open-source mechanism for improving information flow across existing reporting channels, intended to lower reporting barriers and help relevant stakeholders coordinate remediation.
icml-2026-flare-ai-flaw-reporting-for-ai.tldr: FLARE-AI standardizes AI flaw reports and enables optional sharing with multiple recipients from a single submission.

paragraphs: Biophysical neuron models can predict neural activity and responses to electrical stimulation, but fitting their parameters usually requires invasive recordings from inside cells. Electrode arrays can record outside many neurons at once, offering a more scalable measurement method. The challenge is extracting reliable parameters for complex Hodgkin–Huxley models from those extracellular signals.

The paper combines differentiable biophysical simulation with simulation-based inference to estimate model parameters from designed features of electrode-array recordings. Its central application is predicting whether neurons will spike under candidate stimulation patterns. If these predictions are accurate, a model fitted from brief recordings can substitute for extensive direct testing of the candidate patterns.

Validation uses hundreds of hours of stimulation and recording data from isolated macaque retina, collected with a 512-electrode array at 30-micrometer pitch. Models fitted using only a few minutes of recording predict previously unseen multi-electrode stimulation responses with 90.6% accuracy. This result supports faster stimulation-response characterization in the studied preparation; the reported validation is on isolated retinal tissue.
icml-2026-learning-biophysical-models-of.tldr: Biophysical models fitted from brief extracellular recordings predict unseen retinal stimulation responses with 90.6% accuracy.

paragraphs: Removing an object from a video requires filling its former location with content that fits the scene and remains consistent across frames. The paper argues that beginning generation from Gaussian noise wastes useful structure already present in the source video. It instead formulates removal as a direct translation between videos.

A stochastic bridge defines a probabilistic path from the original video to a version with the object removed. This gives generation access to the input’s structural and contextual information throughout the transformation. However, a strong connection to the source can make large objects harder to erase. An adaptive mask modulation mechanism adjusts input embeddings according to mask characteristics, balancing preservation of the background with freedom to generate replacement content.

The authors report significant improvements over existing methods in both visual quality and temporal consistency. The findings support using the original video as an active source of guidance for removal. The mask-dependent adjustment is central to that design because the amount of source information worth retaining can conflict with the amount of change needed.
icml-2026-learning-stochastic-bridges-fo.tldr: A stochastic video-to-video bridge uses source-video structure and adaptive mask modulation to improve object removal and temporal consistency.

paragraphs: A fixed benchmark can become outdated or increasingly familiar to models, making its scores less informative over time. Updating it introduces another difficulty: new versions must still measure comparable capabilities. MMBench-Live addresses both concerns through an automated pipeline that continually constructs new multimodal evaluation examples.

The pipeline uses multiple agents to combine structured task specifications, feedback-guided data collection, and question-answer generation supported by executable reasoning. To keep successive versions comparable, it extracts task-related visual patterns from the original benchmark and uses them to guide collection and filtering. This makes benchmark renewal a constrained construction process tied to the abilities the benchmark was designed to assess.

Built from MMBench, the resulting benchmark contains 5.9K new instances with a high answer-correctness rate. Each update costs about $30 and takes one to two hours. Evaluations show stable model rankings, continued semantic alignment with the original benchmark, and weaker signals of contamination-related memorization. These results suggest that automated renewal can preserve useful comparability while reducing some problems associated with static evaluation.
icml-2026-mmbench-live-a-continuously-ev.tldr: MMBench-Live automatically refreshes multimodal evaluation data while preserving comparable rankings and showing weaker memorization signals.

paragraphs: Formal mathematics systems often coordinate models and tools through specialized pipelines. Numina-Lean-Agent explores a more general approach: using a coding agent directly as the mathematical reasoner. The motivation is to support reasoning tasks beyond theorem proving while avoiding dependence on a separately trained formal prover.

The system combines Claude Code with Numina-Lean-MCP. Through this interface, the agent can interact autonomously with Lean, retrieve relevant theorems, and use informal proving and auxiliary reasoning tools. The design makes specialized capabilities accessible through a general agent interface. It also allows the underlying model to be replaced without training, providing a route to improve performance as base models improve.

Using Claude Opus 4.5, Numina-Lean-Agent solves all 12 Putnam 2025 problems, matching the best closed-source system reported in the abstract. The authors also demonstrate broader applicability by working with mathematicians to formalize the Brascamp–Lieb theorem. Together, these results support the proposed general-agent approach across a competition benchmark and a collaborative formalization task.
icml-2026-numina-lean-agent-an-open-and-.tldr: Numina-Lean-Agent connects a general coding agent to Lean tools, solving all 12 Putnam 2025 problems and supporting collaborative theorem formalization.

paragraphs: Collaborative inference divides a model between an edge device and the cloud, transmitting intermediate representations. Attackers may use those representations to reconstruct the original input. This paper investigates whether choosing the split location can provide intrinsic resistance, avoiding reliance on perturbing the transmitted features.

The analysis argues that depth helps only insofar as it enables a particular representational transition, which is necessary for intrinsic resistance. This transition appears as an abrupt increase in a lower bound on the uncertainty remaining about the input given its representation. A measure of within-class spread, the intra-class mean-squared radius, provides a criterion for locating the resulting Golden Partition Zone. The authors also explain how training and label distributions affect this quantity.

Across four vision models, splits in this zone produce more than four times the reconstruction error of shallow splits. Under enhanced entropy and inversion-model settings, decision-level representations show 66% stronger resistance than feature-level representations. Data type also affects the transition and reconstruction. The results therefore support selecting partitions by representational properties rather than assuming deeper layers alone determine resistance.
icml-2026-partitioning-for-intrinsic-mod.tldr: A representational transition identifies model split locations that empirically resist input reconstruction better than shallow partitions.

paragraphs: Referring expression segmentation converts a textual description into a pixel-level mask of the intended object or region. Multimodal language models have improved this task, but their computational cost is substantial. The authors investigate token compression as a way to reduce that burden and find that typical compression methods can sharply degrade segmentation performance.

Their experiments identify two spatial properties that compression needs to preserve: original position embeddings and local neighborhood structure. PAYN uses this observation to select tokens entirely from position information. It keeps tokens distributed across local regions and preserves their original positional indices, helping the remaining tokens retain consistent spatial relationships.

PAYN is training-free and designed to plug into existing systems. Across multiple referring-expression segmentation benchmarks, it outperforms other token-compression methods. The result supports position-based selection as an effective compression strategy for this task, where output masks depend closely on spatial organization. The claim concerns what information guides token retention; the overall segmentation system still performs the image-and-language reasoning needed to interpret the query.
icml-2026-position-is-all-you-need-a-fre.tldr: PAYN improves token compression for referring expression segmentation by preserving original positions and coverage of local neighborhoods.

paragraphs: Robot world models that predict detailed video can devote capacity to changing backgrounds, lighting, and other appearance details unrelated to control. The paper argues that this can weaken generalization and produce fragile policies. Its Mask World Model changes the prediction target from full-color pixels to evolving semantic masks.

The model uses a video diffusion architecture to predict how these masks change over time. Restricting predictions to masks creates a geometric information bottleneck, directing the model toward physical dynamics and contact relationships while filtering visual distractions. A diffusion-based policy head connects this representation of future change to robot actions, forming an end-to-end control system.

On LIBERO and RLBench, the authors report significant improvements over state-of-the-art RGB-based world models. Real-world experiments also show stronger generalization, and evaluations using random token pruning indicate resilience to lost texture information. These findings support the paper’s central design choice: predicting a representation focused on task-relevant geometry can provide a stronger foundation for control than reproducing detailed visual appearance in the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-predicting-what-matters-robust.tldr: Mask World Model predicts future semantic masks to improve robot control and robustness to irrelevant visual detail.

paragraphs: Voxel-based detectors divide a LiDAR point cloud into three-dimensional cells. With a uniform grid, small objects can occupy too few cells to preserve useful geometric detail. Making every cell smaller increases memory and computation. Radial Scaling Voxelization targets this problem by changing effective resolution according to distance from the sensor.

RSV continuously rescales point coordinates before applying ordinary Cartesian voxelization. This preserves the grid topology expected by existing detectors while creating finer effective cells nearby and leaving distant resolution nearly unchanged. The approach concentrates extra detail in near regions without requiring a globally finer grid. It can replace the discretization component without changing the detector backbone or training pipeline.

Experiments integrate RSV into several voxel-based detectors on KITTI and nuScenes. The authors report consistent improvements for small objects, particularly pedestrians and cyclists, with only marginal additional computation. The findings show that the initial spatial representation can improve detection across different detector architectures, making voxelization itself a useful intervention point rather than requiring a redesigned network.
icml-2026-radial-scaling-voxelization-fo.tldr: RSV improves small-object detection by increasing nearby voxel resolution through coordinate scaling with little additional computation.

paragraphs: Multimodal forecasting methods use numerical histories together with context such as text. Evaluating whether that context helps requires benchmarks that reflect varied real-world situations. The paper introduces TimesX to address concerns about small or synthetic datasets, narrow varieties of textual context, and inadequate mitigation of evaluation data leakage.

TimesX brings together real-world time series across diverse domains and pairs them with textual contexts obtained through an automated generation pipeline. Its contribution is a broader evaluation setting for studying how forecasting methods use accompanying information. The authors use this benchmark for an empirical study of zero-shot multimodal forecasting, examining whether approaches that work on existing benchmarks retain their effectiveness.

The results suggest that many previously successful approaches may fail on TimesX. Meanwhile, simple ensemble methods that use rich textual context can outperform strong baselines on this benchmark. These findings question how readily existing benchmark success transfers to broader evaluation settings. They also indicate that access to useful context, and how methods combine it with forecasts, can matter more than methodological complexity alone.
icml-2026-rethinking-multimodal-time-ser.tldr: TimesX broadens multimodal forecasting evaluation and finds that simple context-aware ensembles can outperform approaches successful on earlier benchmarks.

paragraphs: Test-time adaptation updates a model when incoming data differs from its training distribution. Many approaches select supposedly reliable samples and make their predictions more confident through entropy minimization. The paper identifies two problems: unreliable samples can still enter this process and destabilize the model, while excluding samples can bias the representation of the new distribution.

SaTeen instead aligns test-sample structure with reliable reference structure in two ways. Within a sample, it increases the cross-entropy discrepancy between a reference and a version whose structure has been disrupted, assuming dominant features remain stable. Across samples, it reduces reconstruction error in a reference subspace built using incremental principal component analysis on reliable samples. This second component assumes the underlying data manifold remains stable.

These complementary objectives use both the organization inside individual samples and the shared structure across samples to guide adaptation. The authors report state-of-the-art results across several test-time and continual test-time adaptation scenarios. The findings support structural alignment as an effective alternative adaptation signal under the stated structural assumptions.
icml-2026-sateen-learning-structural-ali.tldr: SaTeen improves test-time adaptation by aligning within-sample and between-sample structure with reliable references under stability assumptions.

paragraphs: Class-incremental learning asks a model to learn new classes over a sequence of tasks while retaining useful earlier knowledge. Extending this process to hundreds of tasks makes the balance between stability and adaptability especially demanding. CaRE addresses this setting by adding a two-level mixture-of-experts routing mechanism to a pretrained model.

The first routing stage selects relevant task-specific routers. The second uses those routers to activate and combine experts. This arrangement aims to supply intermediate network layers with features that are both discriminative enough to separate classes and comprehensive enough to support a long learning sequence. The authors also introduce OmniBenchmark-1K to evaluate class-incremental learning across hundreds of tasks.

CaRE achieves leading results in both conventional settings of roughly 5–20 tasks and sequences ranging from 100 to more than 300 non-overlapping tasks. On the long sequences, the authors report a large advantage over all evaluated baselines. They describe CaRE as the first learner, to their knowledge, to achieve this scale, positioning hierarchical routing as a promising mechanism for much longer continual-learning evaluations.
icml-2026-scaling-continual-learning-to-.tldr: CaRE uses two-level expert routing to achieve strong class-incremental learning results across sequences exceeding 300 tasks.

paragraphs: Conditional independence testing asks whether variables remain related after accounting for other variables. It supports scientific discovery and feature selection by helping distinguish meaningful relationships from spurious ones. Machine learning models can assist these tests, but model-agnostic approaches commonly require splitting data into training and testing portions, reducing statistical power.

Semi-knockoffs accommodates any pretrained model without requiring that split. The method provides valid p-values and false discovery rate control in high-dimensional settings. Its assumptions also differ from approaches that require knowing the full input distribution: for continuous variables, it requires conditional expectations. This narrows the distributional information needed to integrate a predictive model into the testing procedure.

Because conditional expectations may themselves need estimation, the paper develops two theoretical results addressing validity in that situation. One concerns the stability of regularized models trained with a null feature; the other establishes a double-robustness property. The contribution combines model flexibility, avoidance of data splitting, and formal statistical guarantees, while retaining the stated requirements on conditional expectations.
icml-2026-semi-knockoffs-a-model-agnosti.tldr: Semi-knockoffs enables model-agnostic conditional independence testing without a train-test split, with finite-sample guarantees under its stated assumptions.

paragraphs: Recognizing an unfamiliar action from a single labeled example requires a useful representation of how body joints move together. SkelHCC addresses this one-shot setting by connecting skeleton sequences with language descriptions of actions. Its motivation is that human movement has a hierarchy, from individual joints through body parts to the whole body, that ordinary Euclidean representations can struggle to capture.

The framework’s Explicitly Hierarchical Hyperbolic CLIP module places skeleton and language representations in a shared hyperbolic space. The geometry’s negative curvature and expanding volume support the tree-like organization of the joint–part–body hierarchy. A separate language-model-guided voting cache combines information at multiple levels of granularity, providing context-aware one-shot adaptation without additional training for that component.

Experiments on NTU RGB+D 60, NTU RGB+D 120, and PKU-MMD II show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods. These results support combining explicit anatomical hierarchy with language alignment when labeled examples of new actions are scarce. The training-free claim applies to the cache adaptation mechanism, within the broader learned representation framework.
icml-2026-skelhcc-a-hyperbolic-clip-driv.tldr: SkelHCC combines hierarchical hyperbolic skeleton-language representations with training-free cache adaptation to improve one-shot action recognition.

paragraphs: Multimodal language models contain useful semantic knowledge and reasoning capabilities, but adapting them for retrieval can alter the representations supporting those abilities. SLQ investigates how to build retrieval embeddings while keeping the model backbone entirely frozen. The aim is to preserve pretrained representations while learning a small adaptation component.

The method appends shared latent queries to both text and image tokens. Through the model’s existing causal attention, these queries gather information from the multimodal context into a common embedding space. This gives retrieval a trainable interface without changing the backbone parameters. The authors also introduce KARR-Bench to evaluate retrieval that requires knowledge-aware reasoning beyond superficial matching.

SLQ outperforms full fine-tuning and LoRA on COCO and Flickr30K, achieves competitive results on MMEB, and delivers substantial gains on KARR-Bench. These findings support frozen-backbone adaptation as an effective retrieval strategy in the evaluated settings. The contribution connects parameter efficiency with preservation of pretrained structure, while testing the resulting embeddings on both established retrieval datasets and a reasoning-oriented benchmark.
icml-2026-slq-bridging-modalities-via-sh.tldr: SLQ learns shared queries over a frozen multimodal model to produce strong retrieval embeddings while preserving backbone parameters.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning for image editing depends on evaluators that can judge whether an edit was performed correctly. The paper identifies a failure called Attention Collapse: evaluators neglect comparisons between images and miss fine details, leading to inaccurate scores. SpatialReward addresses this by tying evaluation to explicit spatial reasoning.

The reward model predicts edit regions and anchors its reasoning to those locations. This connects judgments about whether an instruction was followed to pixel-level evidence in the relevant parts of the images. Training uses a curated dataset of 260K spatially informed examples. The authors also introduce MultiEditReward-Bench to evaluate editing rewards.

SpatialReward achieves state-of-the-art results on MMRB2 and EditReward-Bench and exceeds proprietary evaluators on MultiEditReward-Bench. Used as an online reinforcement-learning signal for OmniGen2, it yields a 0.90 gain on GEdit-Bench, compared with 0.45 from GPT-4.1, and surpasses the leading discriminative model. These results link more spatially grounded evaluation with improved editing performance, supporting the practical importance of checking where changes occur.
icml-2026-spatialreward-bridging-the-per.tldr: SpatialReward grounds image-editing judgments in predicted edit regions, improving both evaluation and reinforcement-learning gains.

paragraphs: Understanding the geographic context of an image matters for image geolocation and spatial reasoning. This paper examines how different kinds of machine learning models represent that information, focusing on the contribution of textual supervision. It compares vision-only models, vision-language models, and large multimodal foundation models.

The analysis evaluates groups of images containing people, landmarks, and everyday objects. These groups are organized according to how readily their contents can be localized geographically. That structure lets the study examine spatial accuracy across different kinds of visual evidence, rather than treating every image as equally informative about location. The compared families include ViT, CLIP, and models such as LLaVA, Qwen, and Gemma.

The authors find systematic gaps in spatial accuracy and report that textual supervision improves geospatial representations. Their findings suggest that language supplies complementary spatial context useful to visual learning. The contribution is an empirical account of differences across model families and image groups, supporting multimodal learning as a promising direction for geospatial AI.
icml-2026-textual-supervision-enhances-g.tldr: Comparisons across model families and image types show that textual supervision improves learned geospatial representations.

paragraphs: Evaluating a vlog edit involves several subjective judgments, making automated feedback difficult to standardize. The paper develops an evaluation framework with guidance from professional creators and product managers. It separates quality into six dimensions: creativity, consistency, concept design, cinematography, narration, and pacing.

The authors assemble a dataset of 100K vlog edits and introduce VRMBench to assess how well multimodal language models judge editing quality. Their VlogReward model provides scores across the six dimensions alongside actionable feedback for iterative improvement. Its training modifies Group Relative Policy Optimization with an adjustable reward for comparisons between groups, addressing the standard method’s difficulty distinguishing the direction of quality differences.

VlogReward achieves state-of-the-art results and significantly outperforms evaluated multimodal models, including GPT-5 and Gemini-3-Pro. The contribution links a defined evaluation vocabulary, a dataset and benchmark, and a reward model trained to distinguish varied-quality edits. This makes the intended feedback more useful for refinement: creators can receive judgments about particular aspects of an edit together with guidance for improving it.
icml-2026-vlogreward-learning-multi-dime.tldr: VlogReward evaluates six dimensions of vlog editing and provides actionable feedback using a specialized dataset and modified reward training.
